title: Test up to three channels in parallel, then focus on results
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: Which channels to test now, how cheaply, and when one has earned focus, instead of committing to a primary channel before any result.
applies_when: No channel has a first-party readout yet
A working channel's cost is rising (saturation)
exclusions: A channel already works within payback (focus on it; test only as a hedge)
required_inputs: Owner hours and cash cap for tests
evidence_requirements: Current customer sources with rough shares (step 0 audit)
Value per customer computed by code (allowableCac / contribution)
Per candidate: guessed cost per customer, reachable customers before saturation, time to a readable signal, each tagged as a guess
The assumption the test checks (cost, volume, conversion or time)
Reachable audience for the channel, with source
Cost and response trend of the focused channel over successive reads
Evidence of what competitors use (research notes)
Business type, price and margin, buying motion, geography
The goal and why it matters (break-even, capacity, a funding or hiring trigger)
missing_data_behavior: No goal gap: tests still run; skip the needle check.

decision_branches.then: Up to 3 capped tests in parallel (fewer with under about 5 owner hours a week); choose focus at the readout.
Learning result: one optimisation round with a named lever, owner-set band.

decision_branches.if: Channel's reachable volume can't cover the goal gap

implementation_steps: Audit current sources
Brainstorm one specific idea per channel family (see K6)
Attach guessed cost, volume and time-to-test to each idea
Rank into promising, possible and long-shot
Pick up to 3 for the inner circle
Design a cheap test per channel (K2)
Read all tests at their read dates; compare full cost per customer, volume ceiling (K3) and customer fit
Focus on the winner; re-run when it saturates
Write the channel's assumptions in a model sheet
Choose the smallest exposure that can test one assumption
Keep variants few (a handful of ads or pages): testing, not optimisation
Compute the gap in code
For each candidate: reachable audience × rates = customers (funnelCustomers) at P10, P50 and P90
Compare with the gap and the horizon
Brainstorm one specific idea per library family
Mark owner dislikes as bias, not evidence
Score competition from evidence
Map the idea to library IDs
Check the card's fit condition
Pick the card's cheap test
State the goal and its significance
List necessary milestones
Order them by dependency
dependencies: A destination that can convert (page, listing, booking or reply path)
A way to attribute customers to each test (UTMs, unique URL or code, or a 'how did you hear' question)
Conversion tracking or a manual attribution method
A destination that matches the message
A numeric goal with a date (North Star)
Eligibility and price-fit checks still apply
Library eligibility (scoring.ts eligibility) and price fit
A numeric goal with a date

cash_and_labor_requirements.cash: Sum of test caps must fit the monthly budget band
cash_and_labor_requirements.labor: Sum of test hours at or below the owner's stated hours
cash_and_labor_requirements.capability: Tracking per test; owner's own mailbox for any cold email
cash_and_labor_requirements.measurement: Per-test source tagging and a read date

metrics: Full cost per customer per test (spend plus owner time)
Reachable customers estimate vs the goal gap
Cost per acquisition = cost per click / conversion (calc.ts)
Ratio of cost per customer to value
Families represented in the candidate set
Cost per customer trend in the focus channel
Per card: cost per customer, volume, fit
guardrails: Tests have a spend cap, read date and go band; exempt from scaled-ROI checks, never counted in the forecast total.
At least one candidate from each eligible channel family (bias check).
No external action without owner approval
No assumed audience, list, partner or permission
Hard spend cap and stop date
No scaled-ROI forecast from a test (BRP-12)
Verify current platform rules before acting
Reach must carry a source tag
Price fit and eligibility are never overridden by a bias argument
No fake reviews, fake scarcity, misleading stunts
Platform rules verified at execution time
Week-1 list of 5 items or fewer (existing lint)
alternatives_when_constrained: No budget: unpaid tests only (partner placement, community answers, comparison page, owner-mailbox outreach for B2B)
No tracking: unique codes or URLs plus a source question before any test
No owner hours: only channels ClimbOS runs (exec 'auto')
No ad budget: unpaid tests (direct ask to a small site or newsletter, community post, partner placement)
No tracking: unique URL or code
No reach data: a labelled assumption, with the first test designed to measure reach
No competitor research: competition stays neutral (50)
When a card is blocked: the playbook alternatives in contracts.ts
No clear goal: the diagnosis's binding constraint defines the first milestone
stop_conditions: The plan's day-45 decision point (growth-strategy step 10)
Each plan rebuild; when the baseline grows past a phase boundary
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
Parallel tests on the same audience at the same time blur attribution; separate audiences or tracking
Slow-signal channels (SEO, content, BD) lose to fast ones at the same read date; judge them on leading indicators against their own windows (Book 05 §9)
Book-era test sizes ($250 of search ads, a few hundred dollars) are 2014 prices
Low-ticket products: even a 'cheap' test can't show a viable channel (price fit)
Reach estimates for organic channels are guesses; tag them
Overlap between channels (shared audience) inflates totals; ClimbOS already applies PLAY_OVERLAP
Bias-check ideas can become a channel buffet; they're brainstorm entries, not plan entries
An 'underused channel' story invented without research

Dated tactics from the book: like-gated social pages, 'pay with a tweet', freelance long-tail page farms, bought direct-mail lists without checks, copying another product's invite text word for word; verify current platform and legal rules (external_requirement)
An over-pruned path drops maintenance that keeps current revenue (reviews, support)

strategic_preference.rule: proposed: when no eligible channel has first-party results, ClimbOS marks up to 3 top eligible channels as 'test' (not 'primary'). Each gets a cap, a read date and the three questions (cost, volume, fit); 'primary' is assigned only from a readout.

proposed: PB-paid-search-test gains a revise branch. If cost per customer is above value but within an owner-set band and a named lever exists, allow one bounded optimisation round. ClimbOS adopts no default band from this book.
proposed: candidatesFor adds the best eligible channel from each family missing from the top-n, tagged 'bias check', so the agent has to consider or reject it with a reason.
proposed: plans record the goal's significance in one line, and a completed milestone triggers a re-plan prompt.

contextual_heuristic.rule: proposed: when the step-0 audit shows an existing channel supplies most customers below value and isn't flattening, skip new channel tests and focus on that channel.
proposed: a re-run after all tests fail must cite what the failed tests showed (message, funnel step) before adding new channels.
proposed: add an optional 'ceiling' hint per channel (e.g. bounded by list or event size) to the library, used only as a warning, never as a number in owner text.
proposed: competition moves from 50 only with a cited AI delta; prompts forbid 'nobody does X' claims without evidence.
proposed: a focus channel whose logged cost per customer rises across an owner-set number of consecutive reads triggers a Bullseye re-run prompt.

economic_feasibility.rule: proposed: the sum of test caps and test hours is checked in code against the budget and the owner's hours before the plan is shown.

proposed: add play kind 'test' (or intent 'learning_test', as BRP-12 proposes). It is exempt from the P50 'Loses money' error but must carry a cap, a read date, a stated go band and the label that it can't show scaled ROI.
proposed: when a test or play states reach, code flags any channel whose high-estimate customers within the horizon can't cover the gap, and that channel can't be marked primary or focus.
proposed: trade-show and event break-even uses contribution per sale, not price.

missing_prerequisite.rule: proposed: no channel test launches without a source-tagging method.

external_requirement.rule: proposed: platform-specific tactics from this book are verified against current platform policy before use.

unknown_to_investigate.rule: proposed: add library IDs for speaking engagements, publicity stunt (capped moonshot) and customer appreciation.

reconciliation_note: ClimbOS currently picks a primary from priors (scoring.ts select); this versions that (backlog CG-04, CG-05, CG-21, CG-22).
